    z∈Zf​(z)∖(X×{∞})z\in Z_{f}(z)\setminus(X\times\{\infty\}).

It follows that Zf​(z)=X×ℙ1Z_{f}(z)=X\times\mathbb{P}^{1}. This proves Theorem 7.1. ∎

Theorem 7.1 above is the key in the following proof.

Theorem 7.3.

Let X≔𝔸1×𝔾mX\coloneqq\mathbb{A}^{1}\times\mathbb{G}_{m}. Let f:X→Xf\colon X\to X be a finite surjective endomorphism. Then AZO 1.2 and hence ZDO 1.1 hold for (X,f)(X,f).

Proof.

Note that κ¯​(𝔾m)=0\overline{\kappa}(\mathbb{G}_{m})=0. By Lemma 4.2, ff descends along the natural projection π:X→B=𝔾m\pi\colon X\to B=\mathbb{G}_{m}. Hence ff is of the form in Theorem 7.1. The result follows. ∎

Now we are ready for the following two proofs.

Proof of Theorem 1.9.

AZO 1.2 is known when deg⁡(f)=1\deg(f)=1 (cf. [Xie19, Corollary 3.31]). So we always assume further deg⁡(f)≥2\deg(f)\geq 2 for the AZO 1.2 part.

If κ¯​(X)≥0\overline{\kappa}(X)\geq 0, then (1) and (2) follow from Theorem 1.8. Suppose that κ¯​(X)=−∞\overline{\kappa}(X)=-\infty. Then there is an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:X→B\pi\colon X\to B since XX is affine and by the open surface theory (cf. [Miy01, Ch. 3, Theorem 1.3.2]). If κ¯​(B)=−∞\overline{\kappa}(B)=-\infty, then ff descends to an automorphism f|Bf|_{B} on BB of finite order by applying Proposition 4.5. In this case, both AZO 1.2 and KSC 1.3 are vacuously true (cf. Lemma 2.15). So we may assume that κ¯​(B)≥0\overline{\kappa}(B)\geq 0. By Lemma 4.2, ff descends to a surjective endomorphism f|Bf|_{B} of BB. If deg⁡(f)=1\deg(f)=1, then f|Bf|_{B} is an automorphism of BB. We see that d1​(f)=1d_{1}(f)=1 (cf. [Dan20, Theorem 4], arXiv version) and hence (3) holds.

We may assume deg⁡(f)≥2\deg(f)\geq 2 for both (1) and (2). We may assume also that κ¯​(B)=0\overline{\kappa}(B)=0 and π:X→B\pi\colon X\to B is an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle; otherwise, gg is of finite order by Lemma 4.4 and Proposition 4.3, and we are done as before. By Lemmas 4.7 and 2.14, AZO 1.2 and KSC 1.3 are true unless X≅𝔸1×𝔾mX\cong\mathbb{A}^{1}\times\mathbb{G}_{m} (cf. Lemma 2.15). Then (2) follows, and (1) holds true by Theorem 7.3. ∎

Proof of Theorem 1.11.

It follows from Theorem 7.1 by induction on the factors. ∎

8. Maps with larger first dynamical degree: Proof of Theorem 1.12

In this section, we consider Zariski Dense Orbit Conjecture (ZDO 1.1) via the arithmetic degree. Let XX be a projective variety over ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb{Q}} and f:X→Xf\colon X\to X a surjective morphism.

The following is a generalisation of [MSS18, Lemma 9.1] to the singular case, but the proof of [MSS18, Lemma 9.1] is valid even in the singular case.

Proposition 8.1.

Assume that d1​(f)>1d_{1}(f)>1. Let D≢0D\not\equiv 0 be a nef ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier divisor on XX such that f∗​D≡d1​(f)​Df^{*}D\equiv d_{1}(f)D. Let V⊆XV\subseteq X be a subvariety of positive dimension such that (DdimV⋅V)>0(D^{\dim V}\cdot V)>0. Then there exists a nonempty open subset U⊆VU\subseteq V and a set S⊆U⁡(ℚ¯)S\subseteq U(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) of bounded height such that for every x∈U⁡(ℚ¯)∖Sx\in U(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\setminus S we have αf​(x)=d1​(f)\alpha_{f}(x)=d_{1}(f).

Remark 8.2.

Let CC be an irreducible curve which is a complete intersection of dimX−1\dim X-1 of ample effective divisors on XX. Then (D⋅C)>0(D\cdot C)>0.

As defined in [MMSZZ20], an ff-periodic subvariety VV is said to be of Small Dynamical Degree (SDD for short) if the first dynamical degree d1​(fs|V)<d1​(fs)d_{1}(f^{s}|_{V})<d_{1}(f^{s}) for some s≥1s\geq 1 such that fs​(V)=Vf^{s}(V)=V.

Definition 8.3.

We say that (X,f)(X,f) satisfies the SDD condition if there is an f−1f^{-1}-invariant Zariski closed proper subset ZZ of XX such that all irreducible ff-periodic proper subvarieties not being contained in ZZ, are SDD.

Theorem 8.4.

If (X,f)(X,f) satisfies the SDD condition, then ZDO 1.1 holds for (X,f)(X,f).

Proof.

Set ℓ≔dimX\ell\coloneqq\dim X. By the assumption, there is an f−1f^{-1}-invariant Zariski closed subset ZZ of XX such that all ff-periodic proper subvarieties not being contained in ZZ, are SDD.

Assume first d1​(f)=1d_{1}(f)=1. Since (X,f)(X,f) satisfies the SDD condition, there is no proper ff-periodic subvarieties outside ZZ. Pick any point x∈X⁡(ℚ¯)∖Zx\in X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\setminus Z and let Zf​(x)Z_{f}(x) be the Zariski closure of the ff-orbit Of​(x)O_{f}(x) of xx. Then, for some t≥1t\geq 1, ft​(x)f^{t}(x) is contained in a ff-periodic subvariety of Zf​(x)Z_{f}(x) (cf. [MMSZ20, Lemma 2.7]), which is hence either equal to XX or contained in ZZ. In the latter case, xx is contained in f−t​(Z)=Zf^{-t}(Z)=Z, which is a contradiction. Thus the theorem is true when d1​(f)=1d_{1}(f)=1.

Now we may assume that d1​(f)>1d_{1}(f)>1. By the generalised Perron-Frobenius theorem due to Birkhoff, there is a nonzero nef ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor D∈N1⁡(X)≔NS⁡(X)⊗ℤℝD\in\operatorname{N}^{1}(X)\coloneqq\operatorname{NS}(X)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{R} such that f∗​D≡d1​(f)​Df^{*}D\equiv d_{1}(f)D. Let H1,…,Hℓ−1H_{1},\dots,H_{\ell-1} be general very ample divisors on XX. By applying Bertini’s theorem to the pullback of |Hi||H_{i}| to a smooth model of XX, we may assume that C≔H1∩⋯∩Hℓ−1C\coloneqq H_{1}\cap\dots\cap H_{\ell-1} is irreducible and it is not contained in ZZ. By Remark 8.2, we may apply Proposition 8.1 to the curve CC. By the Northcott property, there is a point x∈C⁡(ℚ¯)∖Zx\in C(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\setminus Z with αf​(x)=d1​(f)\alpha_{f}(x)=d_{1}(f).

For some t≥1,s≥1t\geq 1,s\geq 1, our ft​(x)f^{t}(x) is contained in an fsf^{s}-invariant irreducible component VV of Zf​(x)Z_{f}(x) (cf. [MMSZ20, Lemma 2.7]). If V=XV=X then Zf​(x)=XZ_{f}(x)=X and we are done. If V⊆ZV\subseteq Z then x∈f−t​(V)⊆f−t​(Z)=Zx\in f^{-t}(V)\subseteq f^{-t}(Z)=Z, absurd. Thus VV is not contained in ZZ, and is an fsf^{s}-invariant proper subvariety of XX. Hence VV is SDD. So d1​(fs|V)<d1​(fs)d_{1}(f^{s}|_{V})<d_{1}(f^{s}). Set y≔ft​(x)∈Vy\coloneqq f^{t}(x)\in V. Then αf​(y)=αf​(x)=d1​(f)\alpha_{f}(y)=\alpha_{f}(x)=d_{1}(f). Now (cf. Lemma 3.10)

d1​(fs|V)<d1​(f)s=αf​(y)s=αfs​(y)=αfs|V​(y),d_{1}(f^{s}|_{V})<d_{1}(f)^{s}=\alpha_{f}(y)^{s}=\alpha_{f^{s}}(y)=\alpha_{f^{s}|_{V}}(y),

which contradicts Proposition 3.11. This proves Theorem 8.4. ∎

It is clear that the SDD condition is satisfied when dimX=1\dim X=1 and ord⁡(f)=∞\operatorname{ord}(f)=\infty. There are still some nontrivial examples where the SDD condition is satisfied.

Proposition 8.5.

Let f:X→Xf\colon X\to X be a dominant endomorphism of projective variety. Assume either one of the following two conditions.

  1. (1)

    dimX=2\dim X=2, d1​(f)>1d_{1}(f)>1 and d1​(f)≥d2​(f)d_{1}(f)\geq d_{2}(f); or

  2. (2)

    dimX=3\dim X=3, and d1​(f)>d3​(f)=1d_{1}(f)>d_{3}(f)=1.

Then either there is an f∗f^{*}-invariant nonconstant rational function on XX, or (X,f)(X,f) satisfies the SDD condition.

Proof.

Fix an embedding ℚ¯↪ℂ\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}. If there are infinitely many f−1f^{-1}-periodic pairwise component non-overlapping hypersurfaces of XX, then we may find sufficiently many f−1f^{-1}-invariant (not necessarily irreducible) hypersurfaces and hence so does for (Xℂ,fℂ)(X_{\mathbb{C}},f_{\mathbb{C}}). By [Can10, Theorem B], (fℂ)∗(f_{\mathbb{C}})^{*} preserves a nonconstant rational function on XℂX_{\mathbb{C}} and hence so does (X,f)(X,f) (cf. Lemma 2.15). Thus we may assume that there is an f−1f^{-1}-invariant hypersurface ZZ such that for every hypersurface HH of XX, if it is f−mf^{-m}-invariant for some m≥1m\geq 1, then we have H⊆ZH\subseteq Z.

Let VV be any irreducible ff-periodic subvariety of period m≥1m\geq 1. If dimV=0\dim V=0, then we have d1​(fm)>1=d1​(fm|V)d_{1}(f^{m})>1=d_{1}(f^{m}|_{V}).

Assume that (1)(1) holds. We may assume that dimV=1\dim V=1 and V⊈ZV\not\subseteq Z. Hence f−m​(V)=V∪V′f^{-m}(V)=V\cup V^{\prime} for some (nonempty) curve V′≠VV^{\prime}\neq V. Then deg⁡(fm|V)<deg⁡(fm)≤d1​(fm)\deg(f^{m}|_{V})<\deg(f^{m})\leq d_{1}(f^{m}).

Now assume that (2)(2) holds. Since ff is an automorphism, all ff-periodic hypersurfaces are contained in ZZ. So we may assume that dimV=1\dim V=1 and V⊈ZV\not\subseteq Z. Since ff is an automorphism and VV is a curve, d1​(fm|V)=deg⁡(fm|V)=1<d1​(fm)d_{1}(f^{m}|_{V})=\deg(f^{m}|_{V})=1<d_{1}(f^{m}). ∎

Proposition 8.6.

Let f:X→Xf\colon X\to X be a dominant endomorphism of a smooth projective variety of dimension d≥2d\geq 2. Suppose d1​(f)>maxi=2d​{di​(f)}d_{1}(f)>\max_{i=2}^{d}\{d_{i}(f)\}. Then (X,f)(X,f) satisfies the SDD condition.

Proof.

Let VV be any irreducible ff-periodic subvariety of period m≥1m\geq 1. We only need to show that d1​(fm|V)<d1​(fm)d_{1}(f^{m}|_{V})<d_{1}(f^{m}). We may assume that dimV≥1\dim V\geq 1. After replacing ff by fmf^{m}, we may assume that m=1m=1.

Set ℓ≔dimV∈{1,…,d−1}\ell\coloneqq\dim V\in\{1,\dots,d-1\}. Denote by q:N1⁡(X)→N1⁡(V)q\colon\operatorname{N}^{1}(X)\to\operatorname{N}^{1}(V) the restriction homomorphism. Let HH be an ample class in N1⁡(X)\operatorname{N}^{1}(X). Note that q⁡(N1⁡(X))q(\operatorname{N}^{1}(X)) is an (f|V)∗(f|_{V})^{*}-invariant subspace of N1⁡(V)\operatorname{N}^{1}(V).

Suppose the contrary that d1​(f|V)=d1​(f)d_{1}(f|_{V})=d_{1}(f). Then

limn→∞‖(fn|V)∗​(q⁡(H))‖1/n=d1​(f|V)=d1​(f)\lim_{n\to\infty}\|(f^{n}|_{V})^{*}(q(H))\|^{1/n}=d_{1}(f|_{V})=d_{1}(f)

where ∥⋅∥\|\cdot\| is any norm on q⁡(N1⁡(X))q(\operatorname{N}^{1}(X)). Since the cone Nef⁡(X)|V\operatorname{Nef}(X)|_{V} contains an ample divisor on VV, there is some D∈N1⁡(X)D\in\operatorname{N}^{1}(X) such that D|V∈Nef⁡(V)∖{0}D|_{V}\in\operatorname{Nef}(V)\setminus\{0\} and (f|V)∗​(D|V)≡d1​(f)​D|V(f|_{V})^{*}(D|_{V})\equiv d_{1}(f)D|_{V}, noting that d1​(f|V)=d1​(f)d_{1}(f|_{V})=d_{1}(f) by the extra assumption. In other words, we have 0≠V⋅D∈Nd−ℓ+1⁡(X)0\neq V\cdot D\in\operatorname{N}^{d-\ell+1}(X) (the real vector space of codimension-(d−ℓ+1)(d-\ell+1) cycle classes modulo numerical equivalence), and f∗​D≡d1​(f)​D+Ff^{*}D\equiv d_{1}(f)D+F where F⋅V≡0F\cdot V\equiv 0. Since VV is ff-invariant, f∗​V=deg⁡(f|V)​Vf_{*}V=\deg(f|_{V})V. Since f∗​f∗=deg⁡(f)​idf_{*}f^{*}=\deg(f)\operatorname{id} on Nd−ℓ⁡(X)\operatorname{N}^{d-\ell}(X) we get f∗​V≡b​Vf^{*}V\equiv bV where b=deg⁡(f)/deg⁡(f|V)≥1b=\deg(f)/\deg(f|_{V})\geq 1. Then we have

f∗​(D⋅V)=f∗​D⋅f∗​V≡b​d1​(f)​(D⋅V).f^{*}(D\cdot V)=f^{*}D\cdot f^{*}V\equiv bd_{1}(f)(D\cdot V).

Since b​d1​(f)≥d1​(f)>dd−ℓ+1​(f)bd_{1}(f)\geq d_{1}(f)>d_{d-\ell+1}(f), we get a contradiction. ∎

Now we are ready for:

Proof of Theorem 1.12.

It follows from Theorem 8.4 and Propositions 8.5 and 8.6. ∎

Remark 8.7.

The case (1) of Theorem 1.12 is already proved in [JXZ20]. However, the method there is different.

The following example shows that the SDD condition does not hold in general.

Example 8.8.

Let X=ℙ2X=\mathbb{P}^{2} and f:X→Xf\colon X\to X the endomorphism (x,y)→(x2,y2)(x,y)\to(x^{2},y^{2}), in affine coordinates. Then we have d1​(f)=2d_{1}(f)=2. For two coprime positive integers a,ba,b, the curve Ca,b={xayb=1}C_{a,b}=\{x^{a}y^{b}=1\} is ff-invariant and d1​(f|Ca,b)=2d_{1}(f|_{C_{a,b}})=2. This implies that SDD condition does not hold for the pair (X,f)(X,f).
